description: Mitigations for chemical contact and ingestion. Decontamination speed is the primary survival determinant for corrosive exposure. HF requires specific treatment (calcium gluconate).

mitigations.name: substitution
mitigations.description: Replace hazardous chemical with less toxic/corrosive alternative. Water-based instead of solvent-based, citric acid instead of HCl, mechanical cleaning instead of chemical. Inherent safety.
mitigations.pfd_source: Inherent safety — the hazardous chemical is not present.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: Depends on the substitute. Complete elimination if chemical removed entirely. Partial if substitute is less hazardous but not harmless.

mitigations.name: closed_system
mitigations.description: Fully enclosed chemical handling — closed transfer, sealed systems, no open decanting. Prevents skin/eye contact during normal operations.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.03. Failure: seal failure, gasket leak, opened for sampling/maintenance, overflow.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: When system is sealed, no contact exposure occurs. Maintenance/sampling breaks the containment.

mitigations.name: chemical_ppe
mitigations.description: Chemical-resistant gloves (EN 374), goggles/face shield, apron or suit. Material must be rated for the specific chemical. Nitrile for organics, butyl for ketones, etc.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.12. Failure: wrong glove material for the chemical (common — permeation not checked), not worn for 'quick job', gloves perforated, splash over/under PPE.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: When correct material and intact, prevents skin contact. EN 374 breakthrough time gives quantified protection. Gap: splash to face/eyes around goggles.

mitigations.name: emergency_shower
mitigations.description: ANSI Z358.1 emergency shower and eyewash within 10 seconds travel. Immediate decontamination limits burn depth and chemical absorption. THE critical post-impact control for corrosive exposure.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.10. Failure: too far away (>10 sec travel), not tested/maintained (weekly test required), obstructed access, water supply interrupted, worker doesn't use it (panic, doesn't know location).
mitigations.effectiveness_source: Moritz & Henriques: decontamination within 1 minute dramatically reduces burn depth. After 5 minutes, full-thickness damage is established. Effectiveness is entirely time-dependent.

mitigations.name: calcium_gluconate
mitigations.description: HF-specific first aid: calcium gluconate gel applied to HF burn binds fluoride ions, preventing systemic absorption and cardiac arrest. Must be available on site wherever HF is used.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.20. Failure: gel not stocked, expired, not applied immediately (worker doesn't recognise HF burn — initially painless with concentrated HF), incorrect application.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: Calcium gluconate binds F- ions before systemic absorption. When applied within minutes, prevents hypocalcaemia. Delay >30 min from concentrated HF exposure may be too late for cardiac effects.

mitigations.name: labelling_sds
mitigations.description: Correct GHS labelling on all containers, safety data sheets accessible. Prevents accidental exposure from unidentified chemicals. Administrative control.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.15. Failure: decanted into unlabelled containers (the #1 cause of accidental ingestion), SDS not updated, language barriers.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: Labels warn — they don't prevent contact. Effectiveness is indirect: informed worker takes precautions. Prevents the specific 'drank from unlabelled bottle' scenario.
